last.verdict: Snap's profit jumped on cost discipline and subscription growth, but advertising, still most of its revenue, grew only 4%.

takeaways.label: Ads still weak
takeaways.text: Advertising revenue grew just 4%, which Snap itself said is below its ambitions. Brand advertising declined, while performance-focused ads grew strongly.

takeaways.label: Subscriptions carry growth
takeaways.text: Subscription-type 'Other' revenue grew 84%, and paid subscribers passed 30 million. That is why total revenue rose 14% to $1.72B despite slow ads.

takeaways.label: Profit well above forecast
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA (core profit) was $383M, above the $300–350M forecast, and net income was $56M versus a $104M loss a year earlier. Staff is down 13%.

takeaways.label: Bigger Q4 outlook
takeaways.text: Snap guided Q4 revenue to $1.95–1.985B and Adjusted EBITDA to $490–525M, including Specs glasses spending, and trimmed full-year computing costs.

history.verdict: Revenue beat and a stronger Q3 forecast sent the stock sharply higher.

reasons.label: Big revenue beat
reasons.text: Revenue rose 19% to about $1.6B, above the roughly $1.53B analysts expected.

reasons.label: Upbeat Q3 forecast
reasons.text: Snap guided Q3 revenue to $1.70–1.74B and Adjusted EBITDA (core profit) to $300–350M.

reasons.label: Cost cuts, cash, Specs
reasons.text: Post-layoff cost cuts drove $121M free cash flow; Specs AR glasses got a launch date.
